html:
The Ngaanyatjarra are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Western Desert in Western Australia, in the ranges and sand plains near the borders with the Northern Territory and South Australia. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. They belong to the Western Desert cultural bloc, and together with the Pini they have also been called the Nana.

Their neighbours included the Mandjindja and Ngaatjatjarra to the south and east, the Tjalkanti to the west and the Martu to the northwest.

Their country was among the last in Australia to be reached by outsiders. In 1934 the United Aborigines Mission opened a station at Warburton, which drew many families in from the desert over the following decades, while others stayed on their land into the 1960s. Today the Ngaanyatjarra Lands are run by their own council, and communities such as Warburton are known for glass and painting.
